title: Scope and the TDZ

blocks.md:
## A name before it is ready

`let` and `const` exist from the start of the block, but you cannot read them until the line that sets them. That empty stretch is the temporal dead zone. `console.log(label)` above `let label = "east"` throws `ReferenceError`.

`var` is older: it hoists as `undefined`, so a read before the assign is quiet and wrong. Prefer `let` and `const` so the crash teaches you.

On the desk, the fox cannot read a heading sticker that is still blank. Write the heading first, then walk.

blocks.promptMd: What happens if you `console.log(x)` on the line before `let x = 1` in the same block?
Reading a `let` before it is set throws {{a}}.
blocks.explainMd: The name is reserved in the block, but it is not ready. The language throws ReferenceError, not a quiet undefined.

blocks.promptMd: > `readyLabel()` returns `"east"` from a `let` that is initialized before you read it. Print it.

hintLadder.md: A `let` is safe to read only after the line that sets it.
Declare the name, give it `"east"`, then return that name.
function readyLabel() { let dir = "east"; return dir }

description: A name is only alive in its block. Using it too early is a fault.
